== Biography ==

The March Hare is a resident of Wonderland known for his madness; according to the Cheshire Cat, he is as mad as the Hatter, his habitual companion. He keeps house in Wonderland and is customarily found hosting afternoon tea beneath a tree with the Hatter and the Dormouse, the latter being perpetually asleep and serving, by necessity, as a cushion for the other two.

When Alice came upon one of these gatherings unbidden, the March Hare greeted her with an encouraging tone and offered her wine—though she found the table held only tea. He proved impatient with sustained conversation, interrupting to suggest changing the subject because he had grown weary of it. In the dream-reveries of Wonderland, he remains fixed at his never-ending meal, forever sharing teacups with his companions.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dormouse]]''' — companion. The March Hare and the Hatter appear to use the sleeping Dormouse as a cushion at their endless tea table, resting their elbows upon it as they converse.

'''[[Hatter]]''' — fellow host. The March Hare appears to share an endless tea party with the Hatter beneath a tree in Wonderland.

'''[[Alice]]''' — guest. The March Hare appears to receive Alice at the tea table, offering her wine and engaging with her in conversation, though he seems quick to tire of the subject.

''Evolution:''
* [[Hatter]] — Strained friendship (ch.7→ch.11)<ref>Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, chapter 7</ref>
